{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Overloaded Day 1 visits with multiple procedures",
      "quote": "Day 1 (Day 1)",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Day 1 has a high density of procedures including cemiplimab, ISA101b, weight, limited physical exam, vital signs, concomitant meds, hematology, blood chemistry, PT/aPTT, TSH, pregnancy test, urinalysis, PK, ADA, soluble biomarkers, ctDNA, and PBMC. This is burdensome for patients and staff.",
      "fix": "Consider splitting some non-critical procedures to other visits or reducing frequency."
    },
    {
      "title": "Duplicate Day 1 columns in Schedule of Activities",
      "quote": "Day 1 (Day 1) | Day 22 ±3 (Day 22) | Day 43 ±3 (Day 43) | Day 1 (Day 1) | Day 22 ±3 (Day 22) | Day 43 ±3 (Day 43)",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The schedule repeats Day 1, Day 22, and Day 43 columns, which is confusing and likely a typographical error. This could lead to misinterpretation of visit timing.",
      "fix": "Clarify the visit numbering (e.g., Cycle 1 Day 1, Cycle 2 Day 1, etc.) and correct the table."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tight window for Day 8 visit",
      "quote": "Day 8 ±3 (Day 8)",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The Day 8 visit has a ±3 day window, which is tight for patients who may need to travel or have scheduling conflicts, especially given the frequency of visits.",
      "fix": "Consider widening the window to ±5 days if feasible."
    },
    {
      "title": "Frequent blood draws for hematology and chemistry",
      "quote": "Hematology | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Hematology is collected at every visit, and blood chemistry at most visits, leading to frequent blood draws that may be burdensome and increase risk of anemia.",
      "fix": "Reduce frequency of hematology/chemistry to align with key safety timepoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vital signs every hour during 4-hour observation",
      "quote": "Vital signs will also be taken every hour during the 4-hour observation period following ISA101b administration.",
      "page": 66,
      "section": "9.2.3.4 Vital Signs",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Hourly vital signs for 4 hours after ISA101b administration is burdensome for patients and staff, and may not be necessary for all patients.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing to every 2 hours or only for first dose."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tumor tissue sample at screening may be difficult to collect",
      "quote": "Tumor tissue sample for documentation of pathologic confirmation of cervical cancer and HPV16 diagnostic testing",
      "page": 64,
      "section": "9.2.1 Procedures Performed Only at the Screening Visit",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Obtaining tumor tissue may be invasive and challenging, especially if recent biopsy is not available. This could delay screening.",
      "fix": "Allow archival tissue if available and specify acceptable time frame."
    },
    {
      "title": "PBMC collection optional but listed in schedule",
      "quote": "T cell immune monitoring PBMC sample",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "PBMC collection is described as optional in text, but the schedule lists it as a standard procedure, which may cause confusion for sites.",
      "fix": "Mark as optional in the schedule or clarify in footnotes."
    },
    {
      "title": "Adverse event collection only at safety follow-up",
      "quote": "Adverse event |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "Adverse events are only collected at Safety Follow-up, but AEs should be collected throughout the study. This is a critical omission.",
      "fix": "Add AE collection at all visits after informed consent."
    }
  ]
}
